method: Two implementations of the same anchored method: scripts/extract_memory_index_limits.py (the FACTS script, copied here byte for byte) and read_limits() in tools/memory-index-guard/memory_index_guard.py (steps A and B without the script's global-value report, which never decides). Step A binds the line-cap and size-cap identifiers through the loader's user-visible warning template; step B binds their values in the declaration beside the MEMORY.md literal. Either one reports the caps only when both steps bind exactly one pair.
timing_note: Wall time of one run per build on this host, page cache warm; the script's extra time is its global-value scan.
why_step_b: In 2.1.299 the line-cap identifier qN is also declared as 8 in an unrelated chunk, so a search for qN=<int> across the binary finds 8 and 200 and cannot decide; minified names are module-local, and the declaration beside MEMORY.md binds 200.
negative_cases: The FACTS run measured an identifier-mismatch file and an empty file exiting 2. The guard's tests (tests/test_memory_index_guard.py, class Limits) cover those and a missing binary, two different bindings, a computed cap (25*1000), a zero cap and a template without the user-visible anchor: each is unknown, never a number.
fragility: The method rests on three user-visible phrases (lines (limit: ${, index entries are too long, Only part of it was loaded) reworded in 2.1.268, and on integer literals declared right after MEMORY.md. A rewording or a computed cap makes it fail closed (unknown), which the guard reports and does not alert on.
